findings.title: Managed settings are deployed but set no MCP policy

findings.description: Claude Code's managed files in <TMP>/managed set this MCP policy: managedMcpServers provides corp; managedMcpServers entries Claude Code drops: bad name (name has characters other than letters, numbers, - and _); strictPluginOnlyCustomization locks MCP to plugin and managed sources. mcp-audit reads only the managed files in the system directory. An MDM profile, an HKLM registry policy or server-managed settings from the claude.ai console rank above these files and are not visible to it; under Claude Code's default first-wins rule a higher source that delivers any policy key replaces the files' allowlist (deniedMcpServers and allowManagedMcpServersOnly are still read from every admin source, Claude Code 2.1.273 or later; managed-mcp.json always applies).
findings.evidence: files: <TMP>/managed/managed-settings.json
findings.remediation: Confirm the policy is the one your organization intends. Run `/status` in Claude Code to see which managed source is in force, and `claude mcp list` to see what actually loads. Reference: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-mcp
findings.title: Managed MCP policy on this machine

findings.description: Claude Code server 'evil' in .claude.json does not load under this machine's managed MCP policy: managed settings set strictPluginOnlyCustomization for MCP, so 'Users can't add servers through ~/.claude.json or .mcp.json; plugin servers still load' (Anthropic, managed-mcp: Choose a pattern; a value that is neither a boolean nor an array is treated as true, Claude Code 2.1.282 or later). This holds when the managed settings files are the source Claude Code applies: an MDM profile or server-managed settings that deliver any policy key replace them, and mcp-audit can't read those. A server blocked this way disappears from /mcp and claude mcp list with no message saying policy is the reason.
findings.evidence: server: evil (claude-code) | command evil-mcp | reason: plugin-only | file: /h/.claude.json
findings.remediation: Remove the entry, or ask the policy owner to approve the server (add a serverUrl or serverCommand allowlist entry). Reference: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-mcp
findings.title: Configured MCP server that the managed policy keeps from loading
